supersedes.reason: Replication A of registration 0364164c aborted on NATIVE_MENU_MISMATCH: a native menu presented one action id twice. The registration is EXECUTION_INVALID_OR_ABORTED: A consumed and aborted, B not started, no results.

predecessor.rule: The successor is a new registration. It does not continue, resume or complete 0364164c; its unused B namespace is not reused; the consumed A run directory stays as it is and is never rerun.

invalidWhen.EMPTY_MENU: a policy-facing menu has no entry
invalidWhen.DUPLICATE_ACTION_ID: a policy-facing menu presents the same action id more than once

O-6.actionIdentity: The policy-facing action id: on the original view surface[].actionId = canonicalActionKey('R0', action) = forgeActionKey(action) = sha256(stableStringify([actionType, actorId, target, parameters])); on each twin view, that view's own handle (D4: key of the oriented action; IDENTITY: O-2R.1 opaque handle; ORDER: original handle). The descriptor label (e.g. 'forge/bypass') is not identity. Equal ids = the same action.
O-6.policyFacingViews: Exactly the 11 views the frozen connector presents to S0 and Nexus for one world: the original public view, the 8 D4 orientation views (observableView(orientWorld(t, world))), the O-2R.1 IDENTITY view and the ORDER view. Every view is checked; there is no short-circuit.
O-6.validationPoint: Earliest lawful point: after warm-up and after the V3 pre-policy gates (validator, terminal, task, within-run duplicate world, prior-world exclusion, packet horizon), once the post-warm-up world and all of its policy-facing views exist, and before the first policy call and before any evaluator truth exists.
O-6.dynamicContexts: This protocol has exactly one policy decision per world, and every policy-facing menu is a function of the post-warm-up world alone, so all of them are validated before any policy call and the rule is identical for all arms. Evaluator-internal continuation menus are not policy-facing; they are not inspected (inspection would not be outcome-blind) and a duplicate there is decision-inert because the continuation replaces its incumbent only on a strictly higher rank or strictly smaller key. Should a later protocol have policy-facing menus that materialize only after earlier decisions, each is validated immediately before the policy is called on it; an invalid one rejects the whole world atomically for every arm, discards earlier decisions unscored, and is recorded as arm-dependent (menu-validity-v1.mjs atomicDecisionEpisode).
O-6.atomicRejection: One rejection record {id, population, cell, band, reason: NATIVE_MENU_INVALID, cause, firstInvalidView, invalidViews, views, rule}; no selection, menu, truth, metric, nuisance or compute field exists for that world; its world hash enters the within-run duplicate set; it counts in admission like any rejection and is never replaced.
prohibited: repairing, deduplicating, reordering or substituting a native action
reading truth, reward, evaluator state or policy output to decide validity
O-6.otherMenuAnomalies: Not a rejection: a surface that is not a list (NATIVE_MENU_NOT_A_LIST), an entry without a non-empty string id (NATIVE_MENU_ENTRY_MALFORMED), and any remaining frozen nativeLock assertion (NATIVE_MENU_MISMATCH) throw and abort the replication fail-closed.
O-6.precedence: V3 outcomes keep precedence: VALIDATOR_INVALID, TERMINAL_AFTER_WARMUP, TASK_NOT_PRESERVED and PRIOR_WORLD_EXCLUDED rejections and the DUPLICATE_WORLD_HASH / PACKET_HORIZON_MISMATCH aborts are decided first, exactly as in connector-v3.
O-6.delegation: Every world the rule does not reject is passed verbatim to the frozen nativeRowV3, so its row, ledger, rejection or abort is exactly the predecessor's.

changesFromRevision3.ABORT_SEMANTICS: Any exception after the replication directory exists writes ABORT.json (error code only; no world identity, no rows) and re-throws; the replication is consumed; nothing is retried, resized or replaced; analysis refuses while any ABORT record exists.
changesFromRevision3.B_AFTER_A: Replication B refuses unless replication A of the same registration completed and locked without an ABORT record.
changesFromRevision3.NAMESPACES: Not allocated in the candidate. After owner approval, allocate-namespaces-v4.mjs assigns A and B the first two 10^9 blocks from 733 that contain no prior seed and no repository-text occurrence of a seed in their 12,768-seed range; blocks 731 (consumed A namespace, excluded ENTIRELY) and 732 (unused predecessor B, not a continuation) are excluded. The allocation is written once (registration/NAMESPACE_ALLOCATION_V4.json) and bound at activation together with the schedule hashes.
changesFromRevision3.EXCLUSIONS: Full prior exclusions unchanged (9,407 world hashes, prior executed seeds, the 6 OPEN development seeds) plus the entire consumed A block. The consumed A worlds were never recorded and may not be regenerated, so they are excluded at seed level (whole block) only; no outcome of any A world was observed.

conditionalInference: All registered estimands and vetoes are computed on accepted worlds and are therefore conditional on the valid-menu population (as they already were on the V3 validator, terminal, task and prior-world gates).
generalizationLimitation: No claim extends to worlds whose native menu presents one action twice. Under the frozen generator this occurs only when a restore objective re-adds an existing dependency edge that carries an offered BYPASS, which needs a substitute-bearing role (OOD_ROLES only): 1 of 1,824 spent OOD_ROLES worlds, 0 of 7,583 others. Duplicated dependency relationships without menu effect (222 of 9,456 spent worlds) are native generator behaviour visible in every earlier stage; they are not a menu defect and are neither rejected nor repaired.

permittedExecutionEnvironment.runtime: the registration-bound Node binary, versions, platform and launch flags; plain `node campaign-v4.mjs run A|B`
permittedExecutionEnvironment.host: the owner workstation that produced the bound runtime identity
permittedExecutionEnvironment.load: 1-minute load average <= 25% of logical cores; no concurrent stage writer, test runner or campaign
permittedExecutionEnvironment.power: AC power; sleep inhibited (caffeinate) for the run
permittedExecutionEnvironment.process: single process; A then B sequentially; B only after A locked without abort
permittedExecutionEnvironment.memory: analysis <= 1 GiB RSS and <= 30 min per replication (V3)
permittedExecutionEnvironment.logging: full stdout and stderr captured to a file for every run

approvalProvenance: Owner approval is recorded as an explicit conversation instruction, not an independently verifiable cryptographic signature.
